# Project Summary Report

This document is the summary report for the project *"Impostor Syndrome study"* produced during the course "Open Science in Practice: Collaborative Research in Git" held in October 2026 at Karolinska Institutet.

# Objective

The main objective of this report is to describe the characteristics of the FC matrices, demographic information, clinical and acquisition measures of the dataset containing subjects with Impostor Syndrome after data cleaning.

## 1. Data description

This is a descriptive table for `participant_clean.csv`.

```{python}

participants_clean.describe()

```

The table highlights that:

1.  There are no more zeros in IFSS.

2.  The maximum value of `mean_fd` is now less than 0.5 mm.

```{python}

participants_clean_NaN = participants_clean.loc[~participants_clean.isna().any(axis=1)]

print(f"Participants with NaN in their variables: {len(participants_clean_NaN)}")

```

Finally, all subjects with a NaN in one of their variables have been removed.

# 2. Dataset demographics

The sex distribution of the participants included in the cleaned dataset is reported below, including the number and percentage of female and male participants.

```{python}
n_F = len(participants_clean.loc[participants_clean['sex'] == "F"])
n_M = len(participants_clean.loc[participants_clean['sex'] == "M"])
print(
    f"Number of females = {n_F} and number of males: {n_M}\n " 
    f"Female ratio = {(n_F/len(participants_clean))* 100:.1f}%\n "
    f"Male ratio = {(n_M/len(participants_clean))* 100:.1f}%"
    )
```

The age distribution by sex is also reported in this section.

```{python}

sns.boxplot(data=participants_clean, x="sex", y="age", hue='sex', palette='Set2')

plt.title("Age distribution")
plt.xlabel("Sex")
plt.ylabel("Age")
plt.show()

```

## 3. FC distribution

Below the distribution of functional connectivity across subjects is reported.

```{python}

# Extract unique connections, excluding the diagonal
upper_idx = np.triu_indices(len(roi_names), k=1)
fc_values = fc_matrices_clean[:, upper_idx[0], upper_idx[1]].ravel()

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.histplot(fc_values, bins=30)
plt.axvline(0, color="black", linestyle="--")
plt.xlabel("Functional connectivity (Pearson's r)")
plt.ylabel("Count")
plt.title("Distribution of Functional Connectivity")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
